threats.title: Credential stuffing against an unthrottled login endpoint
threats.description: The login route performs a credential comparison with no rate limit, lockout, or CAPTCHA, so an attacker may guess passwords without bound.
threats.attack_scenario: The attacker replays a breach corpus of email/password pairs against POST /rest/user/login. With no throttling, a few thousand requests surface accounts whose owners reused a password.

evidence.snippet: const user = await models.User.findOne({ where: { email, password: hash(password) } })

threats.recommendation: Apply a rate limit keyed by both source address and target account on the login route, and add escalating delay after repeated failures.

threats.title: Session token forgeable from a signing key held in source control
threats.description: The JWT signing key is committed to the repository, so anyone who can read the source can mint a token asserting any identity.
threats.attack_scenario: The attacker clones the public repository, reads the private key, signs a token with the administrator's subject claim, and presents it to any authenticated endpoint.
existing_mitigations: Tokens carry an expiry claim, limiting the window of a leaked token
threats.recommendation: Load signing material from the environment, rotate the committed key, and purge it from git history.

threats.title: Session identifier not rotated on successful authentication
threats.description: No session regeneration was located on the authentication path, leaving the pre-login identifier valid afterwards.
threats.attack_scenario: The attacker plants a known session identifier in the victim's browser, waits for the victim to authenticate, then reuses that identifier to act as them.
threats.recommendation: Regenerate the session identifier immediately after a successful credential check.
